newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa bounces up again after sharp fall.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa bounces up again after sharp fall.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures flipped higher in a late wave of short-covering and trade buying on Friday as the market corrected after taking a pounding a day earlier.
Traders said the upside momentum gathered pace in the afternoon as follow-through spec selling after Thursday's sell-off fizzled out.
The steep fall in Thursday came as specs and funds aggressively unloaded their long positions.
"That has now stopped for the time being," said one trader.
The reversal wiped out values by nearly 15 percent in a week and tentatively ended a dazzling rally that had propelled prices to one year highs.
This morning, support in the market came from trade and manufacturer buying.
"Current prices looked attractive even with the strength of sterling against European units," said one French trader.
As expected, the second quarter Dutch and UK grind data, released earlier on Friday, showed a mixed trend and had little impact.
The Dutch numbers showed a 10.4 percent increase in grind year-on-year to 100,132 tonnes but the UK figures showed a 4.1 percent fall to 42,702 tonnes in the same period.
The German grind data are due to be released next week.
Benchmark September, which plunged to an intraday low of 1,000 stg on Thursday, regained its composure and ended Friday 20 stg up at 1,039 stg a tonne.
Technically, September faces support at the chart gap of between 1,004 and 989 stg. On the upside, the major barrier is pegged at 1,100, which until Thursday was a key support.
But it could struggle to re-conquer this week's peak of 1,170 stg, the top of a rally that started in June when prices were lingering at 1,100 mark.
Volume reached 6,141 lots, again dominated by September and December contracts.
Following the heavy sales on Thursday, September's open interest fell 1,466 lots at 34,891 lots while uncovered positions stood 3,781 lots lower at 23,721.
As of Thursday, the specs were about 16,000 lots long.
The New York market is closed on Friday for the Independence Day holiday, reopening on Monday. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
